summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a slide.
description: `nonSlide(value)` is the same test as `!isSlide(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getObjectId`, `getPageElementById`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a slide; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
const slide = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation().getSlides()[0];

nonSlide({}); // => true
nonSlide(null); // => true
nonSlide(slide); // => false
```
